question: Which Colorado counties apply the homestead exemption to mineral rights?
answer:
Short answer: the exemption follows the claimant's residence, not the minerals [1][2].
- Boulder County courts read the exemption narrowly [3].
- Weld County and Pueblo County treat severed minerals separately [4][5].
- The Tenth Circuit applies the federal rule to bankruptcy estates [6].
- The Ninth Circuit reaches the same result [7].
- The Colorado Supreme Court and Court of Appeals agree on the residence test [8][9].
- The state statute and the federal statute differ in scope [10][11].
- The U.S. Supreme Court has not decided the mineral question [12].

stops.text: C.R.S. 38-41-201 (2024): The homestead exemption protects a dwelling and its appurtenances from execution and attachment. In the memo: the exemption follows the claimant's residence, not the minerals.
stops.label: Colorado State Capitol (C.R.S.)
stops.title: C.R.S. 38-41-201

stops.text: 11 U.S.C. 522 (2023): The debtor may exempt property listed under the applicable state or federal exemption scheme. In the memo: the exemption follows the claimant's residence, not the minerals.
stops.label: U.S. Code / CFR (Washington, DC)
stops.title: 11 U.S.C. 522

stops.text: In re Estate of Hartman (Colorado Court of Appeals, Boulder County (Boulder), 2022): The trial court held that the exemption does not extend to mineral interests severed from the surface estate. In the memo: Boulder County courts read the exemption narrowly.
stops.label: Boulder County (Boulder) → Colorado Court of Appeals (Denver)
stops.title: In re Estate of Hartman

stops.text: Sanderson v. Weld Holdings (Colorado Court of Appeals, Weld County (Greeley), 2021): Severed minerals are personal property and the claimant must record the exemption separately. In the memo: Weld County and Pueblo County treat severed minerals separately.
stops.label: Weld County (Greeley) → Colorado Court of Appeals (Denver)
stops.title: Sanderson v. Weld Holdings

stops.text: Vasquez v. Pueblo Minerals (Colorado Court of Appeals, Pueblo County (Pueblo), 2020): The county court must value the mineral estate before applying the exemption. In the memo: Weld County and Pueblo County treat severed minerals separately.
stops.label: Pueblo County (Pueblo) → Colorado Court of Appeals (Denver)
stops.title: Vasquez v. Pueblo Minerals

stops.text: In re Mineral Estate (United States Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit, 2019): The bankruptcy estate includes the mineral interests, and the exemption applies to the residence only. In the memo: The Tenth Circuit applies the federal rule to bankruptcy estates.
stops.label: U.S. Court of Appeals, 10th Cir. (Denver)
stops.title: In re Mineral Estate
stops.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit

stops.text: Ochoa v. Mineral Trust (United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit, 2018): The panel held that the exemption follows the debtor's residence and does not reach severed minerals. In the memo: The Ninth Circuit reaches the same result.
stops.label: U.S. Court of Appeals, 9th Cir. (San Francisco)
stops.title: Ochoa v. Mineral Trust
stops.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit

stops.text: Holland v. Mineral Bank (Supreme Court of the United States, 2017): The Court declined to decide whether mineral interests fall inside the exemption. In the memo: The Colorado Supreme Court and Court of Appeals agree on the residence test.
stops.label: U.S. Supreme Court (Washington, DC)
stops.title: Holland v. Mineral Bank
stops.court: Supreme Court of the United States

stops.text: Reed v. El Paso Royalties (Colorado Supreme Court, El Paso County (Colorado Springs), 2023): The residence test controls and the claimant need not list the minerals separately. In the memo: The Colorado Supreme Court and Court of Appeals agree on the residence test.
stops.label: El Paso County (Colorado Springs) → Colorado Supreme Court (Denver)
stops.title: Reed v. El Paso Royalties

stops.text: C.R.S. 38-41-202 (2024): The exemption amount is adjusted annually and applies to the dwelling and its appurtenances. In the memo: The state statute and the federal statute differ in scope.
stops.label: Colorado State Capitol (C.R.S.)
stops.title: C.R.S. 38-41-202

stops.text: 11 C.F.R. 522.1 (2024): The federal exemption schedule applies where the state has opted out of the state scheme. In the memo: The state statute and the federal statute differ in scope.
stops.label: U.S. Code / CFR (Washington, DC)
stops.title: 11 C.F.R. 522.1

stops.text: City of Denver v. Claimant (Colorado Court of Appeals, 2021): The city and county of Denver must release the exemption on the recorded deed. In the memo: The U.S.
stops.label: Colorado Court of Appeals (Denver)
stops.title: City of Denver v. Claimant
